ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.label: pilgrims, scholars, the enclave and the river folk
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.summary: Four more peoples of peaceful callings: a fellowship of pilgrims who walk between the shrines and keep hostels, a learned society that keeps an archive and trades in books, a spacer enclave of brokers between the towns and the ships above, and river folk who fish and run the ferries. Each has its own gear, colours, faith, towns and words, and comes to the colony's gate in its own way.
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.tip: They are among the world's peoples when a new world is made, once each, at the game's usual chances; remove them in the world's faction list like any other people. A save made before them meets them when one of them arises during play.
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.description: All four are mostly peaceful. They defend their towns, and they raid only when the colony has turned them hostile, by the game's own rules, and seldom then. Their notables have titles of their own, their messengers words of their own, and their towns a plan of their own when the land suits it.

li.heading: Who they are

table.li: People | Lives by | Age | On the map | Their towns

The pilgrim fellowship | Walking between holy places | Medieval | Cloaks dyed sage, wide cone hats; wardens of the way in one kit with spears | Few: a shrine's court with its flame, and a hostel of bedrolls
The learned society | Books and what is known | Industrial | Claret coats and gowns of every cut; proctors in flak and claret | Few: archives with a reading hall and stacks
The spacer enclave | Trade between the towns and the ships above | Spacer | Pale cyan coats; marshals in one issue of recon armour and charge rifle | Fewest: a market round a landing pad
The river folk | Fishing and the ferries | Medieval | Kingfisher blue hats and coats; river wardens in one kit with fishing spears | Landings on a river bank, with docks out over the water

li.after: With Ideology each keeps a faith of its own (the pilgrim's way, the open book, the exchange, the river's keeping) and its own style; with Biotech each has a share of other kinds of people. With Vanilla Ideology Expanded's memes or Alpha Memes their faiths take a meme of nomads, of the monastic life, of trade or of water too.

li.heading: What they wear, carry and know
li.text: As with the league, the order and the herders, no two of them look alike: each people wears its colour on a piece or two, its soldiers one kit, its civilians whatever their age and calling would, from the game, the DLCs and the mods loaded, and the base game alone dresses and arms every one of them. Pawns already in a game keep what they have.

points.li: The pilgrim fellowship: every pilgrim in a travelling cloak dyed sage, a cape, a robe or a mantle, the cone hat over it, now and then a pack or a banner; the wardens of the way in one kit of helmet and sage cape with spears or pikes; the archers with quivers. They carry a book of the road or herbs. A few are wanderers or minstrels of A RimWorld of Magic, a few wardens paladins and archers rangers, and their keeper is often a priest.

The learned society: fellows and scholars in a claret gown or coat of any cut over a collar shirt, carrying textbooks, novels and schematics; the proctors in one kit of flak under the claret jacket, with guns and, where Vanilla Weapons Expanded's Non-Lethal set is loaded, tasers, dart guns and stun batons. A few are arcanists, enchanters or chronomancers of A RimWorld of Magic, a few have a psylink (Royalty), on a chronopath's or an empath's path with Vanilla Psycasts Expanded.

The spacer enclave: hands, factors and the chair in pale cyan coats over industrial clothes, with tool belts and packs, the chair now and then in psychic finery; the marshals in one issue of recon armour in the enclave's colour with a charge weapon. Hands carry components, chemfuel or medicine. Many of the chairs and some factors and marshals have a psylink, on a harmonist's, empath's, skipmaster's, protector's or warlord's path with Vanilla Psycasts Expanded; a few hands are technomancers and a few marshals psionics.

The river folk: kingfisher blue on their floppy hats, tuques and coats, the rest their own; the river wardens in one kit of blue tuque and plain clothes with fishing spears; fishers with slings and throwing stones, archers with quivers. They carry net cloth, herbs or timber. Their river master is often a druid, a few wardens and archers rangers.

Their kinds of people (Biotech) are a real mix, and still mostly baseliners: every kind with the pilgrims, anima and gauranlen tree folk, the Avaloi, the forsaken and wood elves among them; genies, high elves, the Avaloi and archons with the scholars; starjacks, archons, the Avaloi, lapis and androids in the enclave; coastal merren, nereids, poluxkin and gauranlenkin among the river folk, each where its mod is loaded.

The pilgrim fellowship: at dusk a band of three to five of them may ask the colony for a night's shelter. Taken in, each sleeps in a warm corner indoors and they go on at first light, their eldest blessing the gate, and the colony is glad of it; one night in ten one of them has brought a cough in off the road, and the one who sat up with them catches it. In a holy year their hostel asks the colony for food. Hungry pilgrims, pilgrims to a relic or an anima tree, the great pilgrimage, the holy year and the prophet on the roads come from them likeliest, and their pilgrims, processions, penitents and mourners camp more often.

The learned society: one of their copyists may ask to copy the colony's records for their archive where the colony gathers (a tribal colony's stories, written down), and leave a book in return or teach the colony's best reader while at it. Their caravans carry books, schematics and techprints. A travelling scholar, a book swapper, an old vault opened and the comet come from them likeliest, and their scholars, surveyors and teachers camp more often.

The spacer enclave: when the colony is industrial or later, their factor may call by radio to ask leave to come down by the gate. Bidden, the factor, two to four marshals and the goods come down by drop pod, trade at the gate, and walk off when they are done. Busy orbital lanes and a ship come down come from them likeliest.

The river folk: a boat-trader may bring a catch of the colony's own waters to the gate, for silver or for food from the stores (with Odyssey, whose fish they are). In the spring they ask for timber for the boats, in the summer cloth for the nets. The flood downriver and the ice road come from them likeliest, and their fishers camp more often.

li.heading: Their towns, and new peoples like them

points.li: The river folk's landings stand by a river where the world has one: as a new world starts, a landing the game put where no river runs moves to one within twelve tiles, and with none it stays, its map laid on dry ground. Their landing's map is placed where most of its docks reach the water, and the docks are laid as a jetty over it; with Odyssey its racks hold fish of that water.

The pilgrims' shrine and hostel, the society's archive and the enclave's market are laid out to their plans when a town's map is made, as release A's are; where the land is too wet or rough for it, the game makes its own base.

New peoples that arise during play may take their ways: survivors by a river, and half of them, may become river folk; a band led by a learned one, scholars; a league of spacer-age towns, an enclave; faithful who broke away in an industrial or spacer world, pilgrims. The pace stays as it was.
